findings.evidence: Page 96: "17.5 is the analytical quotient C = 436 ÷ 24.9 before the whole-slot floor, so it is a bound, not a deployable whole-slot count" — immediately followed on page 97 by "(Ch 7, Technical note — per-rank fit: 17.5 GB weights + 54.48 GB KV + 8 GB runtime/NCCL = 79.98 GB of 80 GB)"
findings.issue: Double meaning of '17.5' in two adjacent clauses. On p.96, 17.5 denotes the analytical slot-capacity quotient (436 ÷ 24.9 ≈ 17.51). On p.97, 17.5 GB denotes the per-rank FP16 weight shard (70B/8 = 8.75B × 2 B = 17.5 GB). The parenthetical on p.96 correctly labels 17.5 as 'the analytical quotient C', but the immediately following technical note reuses the same numeral for a weight-shard byte figure without re-labelling, in the same note that the text directs readers to.
findings.fix_instruction: In the Ch 7 Technical note on per-rank fit (p.97), restate the weight-shard figure with its unit explicitly at first use, e.g. '17.5 GB weight shard' rather than bare '17.5', to distinguish it from the slot-capacity quotient C ≈ 17.51 introduced one page earlier.

findings.evidence: Page 164: "~1.31 MB/token 8-bit reference figure from Chapter 1"
findings.issue: Incomplete cross-reference. Chapter 1 (p.7) presents two 8-bit KV figures: ~256 KiB/token for a 7B-class model and ~1.31 MB/token for a 70B-class model. Citing 'Chapter 1's reference figure' without specifying which model's figure leaves ambiguity about which value is being referenced — the 70B figure (the intended one) or the 7B figure.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace 'Chapter 1's reference figure' with 'the Chapter 1 70B-class 8-bit figure (~1.31 MB/token)' to resolve the ambiguity between the two model-specific figures Chapter 1 presents.

findings.page: PDF p. 169 (printed p. 145); conflicting statement at PDF p. 133 (printed p. 110)
findings.evidence: Ch 7 §7.3 'Attention-family sensitivity note' (PDF p. 169): "Real 70B-class dense models commonly use grouped-query attention (GQA): LLaMA-2 70B, for instance, has 64 query heads but only 8 KV-heads, so per-token KV shrinks by the head ratio to KVGQA per-token = 2 × 80 × (8 × 128) × 2 B ≈0.33 MB/token — about 8× smaller."  Ch 5 §5.3(b) (PDF p. 133) states the opposite about the same checkpoint: "(Llama-2 70B is not a GQA-8 example: it uses 64 KV heads, so its per-token KV matches the ~2.62 MB full-MHA form above.)"
findings.issue: The book contradicts itself about the KV-head count of a named vendor model. Ch 5 explicitly rules Llama-2 70B out of the GQA-8 class and says its per-token KV matches the ~2.62 MB full-MHA form; Ch 7 then uses Llama-2 70B as its worked GQA-8 exemplar and derives ~0.33 MB/token from it — an 8× difference for the same model. The two derived constants are used in different sizing contexts (Ch 5 §5.3(b) / Table 5-2 for the Llama-3 70B GQA-8 row; Ch 7 §7.3 for the KV-residency and concurrency-ceiling argument), so a reader who carries Ch 7's number will under-provision the KV budget by ~8× for a Llama-2-class checkpoint. The factual error is on Ch 7's side (Llama-2 70B has 64 KV heads; GQA-8 arrived with Llama-3), so the recurrence sweep confirms the Ch 5 instance as the correct one and Ch 7 as the outlier.
findings.fix_instruction: In Ch 7 §7.3's 'Attention-family sensitivity note', delete the 'LLaMA-2 70B, for instance, has 64 query heads but only 8 KV-heads' clause and replace the exemplar with a GQA-8 checkpoint that the book already treats as GQA-8 elsewhere (e.g. 'LLaMA-3 70B uses grouped-query attention with 8 KV heads of head_dim 128'), or restate it as 'a 70B-class model such as LLaMA-3 70B (GQA-8; note that LLaMA-2 70B has 64 KV heads and would carry the full-MHA ~2.62 MB/token figure, as Ch 5 §5.3(b) notes)'. Then re-check the derived '~3 GB of KV instead of ~24 GB' sentence and the Figure 7.1 caption's '8:1' example so the named exemplar is consistent with the GQA-8 numbers.

findings.evidence: Table 7-1 carries two rows for the same quantity: "KV cache per token (8-bit payload / FP8) | 2 ×80 ×8192 ×1 B ≈ 1.31 MB | = 1,310,720 B = 1.25 MiB; 8-bit here means FP8 (one byte per K/V element), not an INT8 scale-offset layout; reconciles with Ch.1" and, immediately below, "KV cache per token (FP8) | 1.31 MB | = 1,310,720 B = 1.25 MiB; raw tensor byte-halving, exactly 50% of the 16-bit (FP16/BF16) baseline; any block-layout/scale-offset metadata overhead is NOT vendor-measured (see §7.4)".
findings.issue: Duplicate table rows: the same metric (KV bytes per token at 8-bit = 1,310,720 B ≈ 1.31 MB) is printed twice with different row labels and different derivation text. The load-bearing qualifier — that block-layout/scale-offset metadata overhead is not vendor-measured and the 1.31 MB figure is a raw-tensor floor — is attached only to the second row, so a reader who takes the first (earlier, more explicitly labelled '8-bit payload / FP8') row can carry the 1.31 MB constant into a sizing calculation without the caveat. Ch 1 and Ch 6 both repeat this caveat elsewhere ('block-allocation/metadata overhead NOT vendor-measured here'), so the duplication risks three partially-overlapping presentations of one number rather than one.
findings.fix_instruction: Merge the two rows in Table 7-1 into a single row labelled e.g. 'KV cache per token (FP8, raw byte-halving)', keeping both derivations in one cell: '= 2 ×80 ×8192 ×1 B = 1,310,720 B = 1.25 MiB ≈ 1.31 MB — exactly 50% of the FP16/BF16 baseline; 8-bit here means FP8 (one byte per K/V element), not an INT8 scale-offset layout; any block-layout/scale-offset metadata overhead is NOT vendor-measured (see §7.4); reconciles with Ch 1.' Then confirm no other table in Ch 7 repeats the same per-token constant.

findings.evidence: KV cache per token (FP16): 2 × 80 layers × 8192 hidden dim × 2 bytes = 2,621,440 B ≈ 2.62 MB.
findings.issue: Arithmetic check: 2 * 80 * 8192 * 2 = 160 * 8192 * 2 = 1,310,720 * 2 = 2,621,440. The conversion to decimal MB (2.62 MB) is correct (2,621,440 / 1,000,000 = 2.62144). The book explicitly states the SI convention (K=1000, M=1,000,000) in Ch. 4, so this is consistent with its own rules.
Arithmetic check: 9,200 * 2,621,440 bytes = 24,117,248,000 bytes. In decimal GB (1 GB = 10^9 B), this is 24.117... GB, rounded to 24.1 GB. Consistent.

findings.evidence: Total inference KV (9.5K max, resident basis): 9,500 × 2.62 MB ≈ 24.9 GB.

findings.issue: Arithmetic check: FP8 is 1 byte/element. 2 * 80 * 8192 * 1 = 1,310,720 B = 1.31 MB. This is exactly half of the FP16 value (2.62 MB). Consistent.
